front: (HL) Why not multiply by the denominator?
back: Its sign is unknown — a negative multiplier reverses the inequality.

Signs (right to left): $+, -, +, -$. Solution $-2 \le x \le 1$ or $x \ge 4$.
A squared factor does not change sign: $x > -3$, $x \ne 1$.
Critical values $-1$, $2$: $-1 \le x < 2$ ($x = 2$ excluded — denominator zero).

front: (HL) Safe way to clear a denominator $g(x)$ in an inequality?
back: Multiply both sides by $[g(x)]^2$, which is positive (for $g(x) \ne 0$), so the sign is kept.

front: (HL) Can a zero of the denominator be in the solution of a $\le$ or $\ge$ inequality?
back: Never — the expression is undefined there, so use an open endpoint.
Find the intersections on a GDC; the solution is the set of $x$ where the graph of $f$ lies above the graph of $g$.
